newsitem.title: BELARUS: Imprisoned Belarus ex-bank chief in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Imprisoned Belarus ex-bank chief in hospital.

text.p: Former Belarus central bank head Tamara Vinnikova, imprisoned on corruption charges, fell ill and was taken to hospital on Friday after hearing her plea for clemency had been refused, an official said.

Vinnikova, 46, has been in jail since her sacking and arrest a month ago on charges of corruption that were reported to have been instigated by the former Soviet republic's hardline president, Alexander Lukashenko.

"Her condition worsened when she heard the court had turned down her request today to be released from solitary confinement on health grounds," the official at the prosecutor's office, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
Vinnikova wrote to Lukashenko and the prosecutor general protesting her innocence and pledging not to leave Minsk if she were freed on health grounds, Russia's Interfax news agency said.
But after hearing the court had turned down her request, she fell sick -- possibly suffering a relapse from an operation to remove a growth from her abdomen last year, the official said.
"The decision to keep her isolated was not taken once and for all. Her health could be taken into account but it's too soon to talk about that," the official added.
Belarus' state radio said Vinnikova, appointed central bank chief in February last year, had been sacked for causing "damage to the state of major proportions".
The charges are reported to stem from her days running Belarusbank, which merged with the state savings bank in 1995 to create the country's biggest bank.
Interfax quoted an unnamed source at the prosecutor's office as saying Vinnikova was arrested because of "abuse of her position and financial machinations".
She had initially been a strong supporter of Lukashenko's reluctant approach to market reforms, but over time came to oppose many of his policies.
